heading: Backup heads compensate when main heads that copy names are ablated
definition: when the main name-mover heads are ablated, other heads take over their role (self-repair inside the circuit).
summary: Follow-up studies support compensation by other heads under some conditions after the main name-copying heads are ablated in GPT-2 small. Larger models remain unassessed.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 suggested for GPT-2 small at <1B; other scales unassessed. counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size contains '<1B' and 'not stated' only.
suggested_status.reason: Alternative-method results support conditional compensation in GPT-2 small: increased backup attribution and additional freezing costs relative to primary removal without freezing (arXiv:2607.01940#R10, arXiv:2607.01940#R12, arXiv:2607.01940#R13), primary–backup ablation interactions (arXiv:2608.19338#R1, arXiv:2608.19338#R2), and graded backup-head responses (arXiv:2610.02173#ioi-h11-2, arXiv:2610.02173#ioi-h10-2). Distributed compensation supports V2; freezing losses do not partition total repair. Small predictive gains over a mask distribution including complete primary removal do not establish incomplete compensation (arXiv:2608.19338#R8, arXiv:2608.19338#R9). Interpreting increased contributions as release of standing coupling also supports V2, which does not require newly recruited functionality. Supplied counts: versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies = 8; versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1; versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. These aggregate counts precede the checker's verdict corrections and do not establish author independence for the named examples. R2 remains provisional pending that verification.
suggested_status.open_questions: Verify author independence of the named replications; test matched interventions on L10H6; measure individual backup attention and performance recovery together; and test explicitly identified larger models and other families. Matched failures or evidence that the compensation is an intervention artifact would change the assessment.

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The authors ablated all Name Mover Heads (heads that copy names into the output) in GPT-2 small and used path patching to test other heads’ effects on output scores.
original_result.result: The mean IOI logit difference dropped by 5%, and the task still worked. Eight selected Backup Name Mover Heads compensated for the loss of the main heads.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Backup heads increased name copying after the three main name movers were ablated.
Backup heads began copying names when the earlier name-mover stage was removed.
Ablation recruited backups; compensation persisted and strengthened during fine-tuning on uncorrupted indirect-object identification examples.
Removing core name movers increased other heads' contributions and weakened heads' opposition to name copying.
Joint primary and backup ablation shrank the answer score gap more than their summed effects predicted.
Holding later heads' outputs constant revealed compensation masking primary name movers' effects in GPT-2 small.
Different interventions elicited similar backup behavior, and backups for backup heads were reported.
Backup heads contributed more, largely preserving the gap between answer scores after primary name-mover ablation.
Weaker opposition from heads inhibiting name copying explained 39% of performance recovery after name-mover ablation.
Some backup heads remained unresponsive, while compensation reflected coupling already present before ablation.
Backup effects concentrated at complete primary removal, with small predictive gains across held-out masks.
After copying heads were ablated, backups took over while heads opposing copying suppressed it less.
Compensation extended beyond the eight documented backup heads after primary name-mover removal.

untested.what: Backup takeover in explicitly identified non-GPT-2 families and at larger model scales.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_family lists GPT-2 and 'other or not stated'; versions.V2.studies_by_size lists only '<1B' and 'not stated'. The unspecified-model rows arXiv:2402.15390#R2 and lw:hhhmcWkgLwPmBuhx7#r1 do not establish another family or scale.

untested.what: Emergence of backup compensation during pretraining, its training cause, and takeover in instruction-tuned or reasoning models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_stage contain only 'not stated' and 'fine-tuned'. The original lists the origin of compensation as untested; arXiv:2503.01896#R10 and #R11 cover clean-IOI fine-tuning rather than pretraining emergence or a causal test of the dropout hypothesis.

untested.what: Whether the IOI backup-head mechanism transfers to other tasks.
untested.basis: The original explicitly lists behavior beyond IOI as untested. The V2-linked rows concern IOI; counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation documents intervention coverage but does not establish cross-task transfer. General-language-model self-repair discussed in arXiv:2402.15390 is not a V2 test of transferring these IOI backup roles.

wording_issues.phrase: other heads take over their role
wording_issues.issue: In GPT-2 Small IOI with the three Name Mover heads ablated, negative heads contribute 39% of self-repair through reduced suppression. Increased backup name moving therefore describes part of the repair mechanism; the phrase should not be read as an exhaustive explanation of self-repair.

wording_issues.phrase: when the main name-mover heads are ablated
wording_issues.issue: The evidence combines complete primary removal, removal of L9H9 alone in GPT-2-small fine-tuned on clean IOI for 3 epochs, a dosed core that leaves another primary free, residual-stream transfer, and indirect witness scoring. These interventions should not be presented as interchangeable tests. The dose study's standing-coupling interpretation supports compensation and does not itself qualify V2.

method_sensitivity.what: The primary–backup interaction remains positive under both replacements but differs in magnitude: 1.080 logits for template-conditioned mean ablation and 1.268 for zero ablation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direct group-ablation interactions versus held-out subset prediction
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2-small, original-template mean ablation gives a direct primary–backup interaction of 1.055 logits. Adding the primary–backup term to the response model improves held-out MAE from 0.386 to 0.377, with reported improvement 0.0083, and predictive R² from 0.752 to 0.774. Prediction uses mean activation replacement, one IOI template, 256 name pairs, 240 masks (239 non-clean masks scored), and five-fold held-out evaluation. Masks are stratified by exact primary-removal count, with at least two removed primaries oversampled; the distribution includes complete primary removal. These prediction scores measure predictive usefulness over that distribution; incomplete compensation after complete primary removal is cannot_determine, and these results do not establish a limitation of V2.

L11.h10 has a curved, uncertified response under the L9.h6 + L9.h9 core. Adding L10.h7 to the clamped core yields slope −0.2695 and R² 0.972. The intervention set changes which response is detected and its shape.

Primary Name Mover importance changes from NIE 0.14 to witness-integrated score 1.16. Generic downstream compensation can mask primary importance, but these scores do not independently establish named-backup takeover.

In GPT-2-small IOI, the reference condition after primary-set zero ablation without freezing has IOI margin 2.290 ± 0.110. Freezing documented backups at intact-state activations causes an additional margin loss of 0.57 ± 0.09; freezing the CoAx-selected set causes an additional loss of 0.90 ± 0.07. The CoAx set only partly overlaps the documented backups, so measured load-bearingness depends on set selection. These freezing losses are not partitions of total repair and do not establish a limitation of V2.
